name: S1 Visa (family of a foreign worker or student, long-term)

requirement_groups.name: Family of a work- or study-visa holder

requirements.blocker_text: The sponsoring family member must hold a valid Z (work) or long-term X1 (student) visa/residence permit; S1 covers stays exceeding 180 days, while the related S2 status covers shorter visits under 180 days.
requirements.fix_path: Wait until the sponsoring family member holds a qualifying Z or X1 status.

requirements.blocker_text: Covers spouses, minor children, parents, and parents-in-law of the sponsoring foreign worker or student.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate, birth certificate, or documentation proving the qualifying family relationship
Sponsor's valid Z or X1 visa/residence permit

outcome.duration_length: tied to the sponsor's visa validity, converted to a Residence Permit for Private Affairs after arrival

sources.title: China Neighbor -- China Visa Types: Complete Guide for Foreigners (2026), describing S1/S2 eligibility

notes: Structurally similar to Korea's F-1/F-3 family-of-a-foreign-resident route: no direct path to permanent residence or citizenship, since it depends entirely on the sponsor's own (also non-citizen) status rather than on Chinese citizenship or permanent residence. leads_to_pr is correctly false, not merely unpopulated -- unlike cn_q1_family_reunion, which can lead to Chinese permanent residence via the spouse-of-citizen track, S1 dependents have no independent route to settlement documented in sources checked for this build; if the sponsor eventually obtains Chinese permanent residence, the family would need to separately qualify under cn_q1_family_reunion rather than S1 itself carrying forward. switchable_to is empty for the same reason -- there is no direct route-graph progression from S1 to another status in this dataset's model, only a contingent path through the sponsor's own status change. HONEST SOURCING GAP: same tier-3-only basis as the other short-notice entry visas in this build.
